Header: Maize streak virus Chikanga cha mchimanga

Prevention: MH 26, MH 27, MH 28, Pan 4M-19, SC 403, SC 627 and
Maize streak virus is not spread mechanically or through seed but it is good practice to plant certified disease-free seed.
Plant early with the first rains to avoid large populations of the vector (psyllid/leafhopper) which spread the disease.
Rotate maize with non-cereals such as legumes and cassava.
Avoid overlap of two maize crops.
Keep fields free from weeds, especially grass weeds which act as alternative hosts.
Monitoring: Inspect the maize plants regularly for the symptoms of the disease every week.
Look for early disease symptoms such as small, round scattered yellow/white spots or flecks on the leaves which enlarge parallel to leaf veins.
The growth of the plants may also be stunted.
Leaves formed after infection develop chlorosis of broken yellow streaks parallel to the veins which differ from the dark green of normal foliage.
Direct Control: Remove the source of inoculum - uproot, burn or feed to livestock all infected plants as soon as they are noticed.
Uprooting is particularly effective when practiced during early stages of infection in the maize field.
Restrictions: There are no chemical controls for this disease.
Chemical insecticides (such as cypermethrin, imidacloprid and dimethoate) may be used to control the insect vector but this may not be economically viable for small scale farmers
